In [[geometry]], a '''tetrakis hexahedron''' (also known as a '''tetrahexahedron''', '''hextetrahedron''', '''tetrakis cube''', and '''kiscube'''{{r|cbg}}) is a [[Catalan solid]]. Its dual is the [[truncated octahedron]], an [[Archimedean solid]].<ref name=":0" />

It can be called a '''disdyakis hexahedron''' or '''hexakis tetrahedron''' as the [[Dual (polyhedron)|dual]] of an [[omnitruncated]] [[tetrahedron]], and as the [[barycentric subdivision]] of a tetrahedron.{{r|ls}}
[[File:Tetrakis hexahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a tetrakis hexahedron]]

== As a Kleetope ==
The name "tetrakis" is used for the [[Kleetope]]s of polyhedra with square faces.{{r|cbg}} Hence, the tetrakis hexahedron can be considered as a [[cube]] with [[square pyramid]]s covering each square face, the Kleetope of the cube. The resulting construction can be either convex or non-convex, depending on the square pyramids' height. For the convex result, this solid comprises twenty-four isosceles triangles.{{r|kd}} A non-convex form of this shape, with [[equilateral triangle]] faces, has the same surface geometry as the [[regular octahedron]], and a paper octahedron model can be re-folded into this shape.{{r|rus}} This form of the tetrakis hexahedron was illustrated by [[Leonardo da Vinci]] in [[Luca Pacioli]]'s ''[[Divina proportione]]''.{{r|pacioli}}

[[File:Pyramid_augmented_cube.png|thumb|center|Non-convex tetrakis hexahedron with equilateral triangle faces]]

Denoting the edge length of the base cube by {{tmath|a}}, the height of each pyramid summit above the cube is {{tmath|\tfrac{a}{4} }}. The inclination of each triangular face of the pyramid versus the cube face is <math>\arctan\tfrac{1}{2} \approx 26.565^\circ</math> {{OEIS|A073000}}. One edge of the [[Triangle|isosceles triangles]] has length {{mvar|a}}, the other two have length {{tmath|\tfrac{3a}{4},}} which follows by applying the [[Pythagorean theorem]] to height and base length. This yields an altitude of <math>\tfrac{\sqrt 5 a}{4}</math> in the triangle ({{OEIS2C|A204188}}). Its [[Triangle#Computing the area of a triangle|area]] is <math>\tfrac{\sqrt 5 a^2}{8},</math> and the internal angles are <math>\arccos\tfrac{2}{3} \approx 48.1897^\circ</math> and the complementary <math>180^\circ - 2\arccos\tfrac{2}{3} \approx 83.6206^\circ.</math> The [[Pyramid (geometry)#Mensuration|volume of the pyramid]] is {{tmath|\tfrac{a^3}{12};}} so the total volume of the six pyramids and the cube in the hexahedron is {{tmath|\tfrac{3a^3}{2}.}}

This non-convex form of the tetrakis hexahedron can be folded along the square faces of the inner cube as a [[net (geometry)|net]] for a four-dimensional [[cubic pyramid]].

== As a Catalan solid ==
{{multiple image
 | align = right  | total_width = 300
 | image1 = Perspectiva Corporum Regularium 15d.jpg
 | image2 = Dual compound truncated 8 max.png
 | footer = [[Dual compound]] of [[truncated octahedron]] and tetrakis hexahedron. The woodcut on the left is from ''[[Perspectiva Corporum Regularium]]'' (1568) by [[Wenzel Jamnitzer]].
}}
The tetrakis hexahedron is a [[Catalan solid]], the [[dual polyhedron]] of a [[truncated octahedron]]. The truncated octahedron is an [[Archimedean solid]], constructed by cutting all of a [[regular octahedron]]'s vertices, so the resulting polyhedron has six squares and eight hexagons.{{r|williams}} The tetrakis hexahedron has the same symmetry as the truncated octahedron, the [[octahedral symmetry]].{{r|mclean}}

[[Cartesian coordinates]] for the 14 vertices of a tetrakis hexahedron centered at the origin, are the points 
<math display=block>
  \bigl( {\pm\tfrac32}, 0, 0 \bigr),\  
  \bigl( 0, \pm\tfrac32, 0 \bigr),\ 
  \bigl( 0, 0, \pm\tfrac32 \bigr),\ 
  \bigl({\pm1}, \pm1, \pm1 \bigr).
</math>

The length of the shorter edges of this tetrakis hexahedron equals 3/2, and that of the longer edges equals 2. The faces are acute isosceles triangles. The larger angle of these equals <math>\arccos\tfrac19 \approx 83.62^{\circ}</math> and the two smaller ones equal <math>\arccos\tfrac23 \approx 48.19^{\circ}</math>.

The tetrakis hexahedron is [[K-vertex-connected graph|4-connected]]: every three of the vertices separate from the remaining vertices, and the graph remains connected. Every 4-connected polyhedron can be realized as the [[ideal polyhedron]], and the tetrakis hexahedron is such.{{r|ds}}

== Applications ==
{{unreferenced section|date=May 2025}}
Naturally occurring ([[crystal]]) formations of tetrahexahedra are observed in [[copper]] and [[fluorite]] systems.<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last=Klein |first=Cornelis |title=Manual of Mineral Science |last2=Dutrow |first2=Barbara |publisher=Wiley |year=2007 |edition=23rd |page=378}}</ref>

[[Polyhedral dice]] shaped like the tetrakis hexahedron are occasionally used by [[gamer]]s.

A [[24-cell#Projections|24-cell]] viewed under a vertex-first [[perspective projection]] has a surface topology of a tetrakis hexahedron and the geometric proportions of the [[rhombic dodecahedron]], with the rhombic faces divided into two triangles.

The tetrakis hexahedron appears as one of the simplest examples in [[Building (mathematics)|building]] theory. Consider the [[Riemannian symmetric space]] associated to the [[Group (mathematics)|group]] [[Special linear group|''SL''<sub>4</sub>('''R''')]]. Its [[Tits metric|Tits boundary]] has the structure of a [[Building (mathematics)#Spherical building|spherical building]] whose apartments are 2-dimensional spheres. The partition of this sphere into spherical [[simplex|simplices]] (chambers) can be obtained by taking the radial projection of a tetrakis hexahedron.

== Symmetry ==
{{unreferenced section|date=May 2025}}
With [[tetrahedral symmetry]], the triangular faces represent the 24 fundamental domains of tetrahedral symmetry.{{r|rr}} This polyhedron can be constructed from six [[great circle]]s on a sphere. It can also be seen by a cube with its square faces triangulated by their vertices and face centers, and a tetrahedron with its faces divided by vertices, mid-edges, and a central point.
